paragraphs: Keshemmoleach habbasar lehaplit haddam shello kede lebashshelo, tzarik lemalecho mishshene tzedadim; veim hachatika aba, en tzarik lechatekah lishniyyim. veyizzaher lepazzer alayv melach bekullo, shello yishshaer bo maqom belo melach. ubediabad im lo pizzer melach bekullo mammash - kevan demelach mishshene tzedadim, muttar. vetzarik sheyyimlachennu ad kede shello yehe rauy leekol im oto melach. veen tzarik leharbot alayv melach beyoter sheyyihyeh alayv melach ab kebinyan; veraq tzarik ledaqdeq lepazzer al kullo, shello yehe maqom panuy belo melach. vehaopot ushear chatikot hachalulim, tzarik lemalecham gam mibbipnim. veken yizzaher liqroa haopot mitztzad echad, kullo o rubbo; velo keotam shennohagim laasot raq neqeb qatan baop kede lehotzi habbene-meayim, molechin; ki ellu enam yekolim limloach yapeh mibbipnim.

clarification.explanation: When salting meat to draw out its blood before cooking, it must be salted on both sides, and a thick piece need not be cut. The salt should be scattered over the entire surface of the meat so no spot is left unsalted (after the fact, if salted on both sides even without scattering everywhere, it is permitted), until it would be unfit to eat with that salt (no need for a thick layer of salt). Fowl and hollow pieces are also salted internally, and therefore the fowl should be split open on one side rather than relying on a small hole, since through a small hole it is impossible to salt the inside properly.
takeaways: Salt on both sides, scattered over the entire surface.
Fowl and hollow pieces are salted internally too, by splitting them open rather than through a small hole.

paragraphs: Im lo malach haopot mibbipnim ella raq malach mibbachutz, veken chatikat basar shello nimlecha ella mitztzad echad davqa - "g demaran za"l mattir bediabad, tzarik lehorot kisbarat harama" deoser bediabad; veraq behepsed merubbeh o bishat haddechaq likbod shabbat, yesh lehattir kisbarat maran za"l. veayyen "minchat-yaaqob", kelal t"v, seip qatan t"v, v"erek-hashshulchan", ot ch'. vaapillu im hatztzad shennimlach hinnicho lematta, yesh lehattir behepsed merubbeh. veayyen "pitche-teshuba" v"yd-eprayim". umihu opot shello nimlechu ella mitztzad echad mibbipnim umibbachutz, dehaynu shello nimlach ella tzela echad shel haop, abal hatztzela hashsheni nishar kullo beli melicha - hen mibbachutz, hen mibbipnim - hare zeh asur apillu bediabad gam ledaat mera"n za"l; vaapillu behepsed merubbeh name asur, mippene shehechalal mapsiq, veen haddam shebbatztzela hashsheni nigrar veyotze. veda d"g shekkatabnu bachatika shennimlecha mitztzad echad, veken beopot shennimlechu mibbachutz davqa, deyesh lehattir bediabad behepsed merubbeh o tzorek gadol - haynu davqa im nitbashshel habbasar, abal im adayin lo nitbashshel, lo yebashshelennu, ella kak yaaseh: deim hu tok y"b shaot shennimlach ukebar huddach achar melicha, denistemu niqbe happelita shebbo - az yachzor veyimlachennu meshanne tzedadim, kede shetztzad hashsheni yiplot tzir dideh; veim lo huddach achar hammelicha, en tzarik limloach ella raq hatztzad hashsheni shello nimlach. veayyen mishbetzot zahab vechavvot daat. veim hu achar y"b shaot meet shennimlach, az taqqanato hu sheyyitzlennu, denura mashab shaab; uben im huddach, uben im lo huddach, muttar bekol gavna. veayyen keneset haggedola, haggahat habbet yosep, ot qt"v. v"g deharab "yad-eprayim" asa taqqana lebashshelo gam ken hinneh haggaon sipte daat lo samak al zeh lehattir, vekannizkar bisip qatan k"g. veod - harab "yad-eprayim" asa tenay betaqqanat habbishshul, lehashgicha beet hammelicha shello yithappek, ayyen sham; veyesh lachush shemma lo yashgicha yapeh bazeh, laken taqqanato hu bitzliyya davqa.

clarification.explanation: A fowl salted only from outside, or a piece salted on only one side — although Maran permits it after the fact, one should rule like the Rema, who forbids it after the fact, permitting it as Maran does only in a case of great loss or for the sake of the Sabbath. But a fowl salted only on one side of the ribcage (inside and out) while the other side received no salting at all is forbidden even after the fact and even in great loss, since the cavity interrupts and the blood is not drawn out. And the entire leniency after the fact applies only if it has already been cooked; if not yet cooked, one should not cook it — unless within twelve hours of the salting it was already rinsed (thereby sealing the pores that release blood), in which case it should be salted again on both sides; and if not rinsed, only the unsalted side should be salted again (and if twelve hours have passed since the salting, the remedy is specifically roasting, since the fire draws out the blood). And although some proposed a remedy of cooking it instead of roasting, provided one watches carefully during salting that the meat does not turn over, this remedy was not relied upon halachically, out of concern the watching might not be adequate — and therefore the practical remedy is roasting alone.
takeaways: Salted on one side only — forbidden after the fact, with leniency only in great loss.

Not yet cooked — salt again; after twelve hours, roasting specifically is required, and a proposal to cook it under careful watching is not relied upon, out of concern the watching would be inadequate.

paragraphs: Harosh choteko lishniyyim, umotzi et hammocha mittok haggulgolet veqorea et haqqerum, umoleach hammocha, vechotek haggulgolet sheti vaereb, umoleach harosh yapeh letzad panim, vechozer umoleach oto mibbachutz al hassear, sheen hassear meakkeb "y hammelach lehaplit haddam. veim lo chatak et harosh lishniyyim, velo hotzi hammocha meetzem haggulgolet, ella raq naqab et etzem haggulgolet, shari. veayyen sipte daat umachaziq beraka veod acharonim; udelo keharab "bet-yaaqob" za"l. veim chatako lishniyyim umalach mitztzad happanim bilbad velo mitztzad hashsheni shel hassear - dino kedin chatikat basar shennimlecha mitztzad echad bilbad shekkatabnu leel. veda ki derek zeh shel chatikat harosh lishniyyim vehotzaat hammocha meetzem haggulgolet noheg gam baop; ella shebbaop, derek haolam lehashlik harosh mechamat geriuto, veen mebashshelim oto; veraq poh irenu bagdad y" yesh lahem minhag qadmon, shemmebiim im hakkalla keshettelek mibbet abiha lebet balah belel harishona shel hachuppa tarnegol vetarnegolet shechutin umebushshalim, umaqpidim lebashshelam im harosh shellahem, ki iqqar hassiman tob shellahem hu bazeh. vaani amarti shezzeh hamminhag nitqan mizzeman qadmon, shehaya minhagam leholik im hechatan vekalla tarnegol vetarnegolet chayyim, siman lipriyya urebiyya; veyatza mizzeh taqqala shennecherab tur-malka venehergu kamma nepashot, kidita begittin, dap n"z (ammud ). veyittaken achar meora hahu batelu hamminhag leholik chayyim, vehayu molikin shechutim umebushshalim. veek sheyyihyeh - minhag zeh yeshno beirenu; vekevan shehem maqpidim lebashshelam im harashim shellahem, tzarik lehazhiram sheyyihyu noqebim qodem melicha et etzem haggulgolet, veshari.

clarification.explanation:
The head is cut in two, the brain is removed from the skull, the membrane is torn, and the brain is salted; the skull is cut lengthwise and widthwise, salted well inside and also outside over the hair (since the hair does not prevent the salt from drawing out the blood). And if the head was not cut in two and the brain not removed, but only the skull bone was perforated — it is permitted. And if it was cut in two and salted only on the inside, not on the hair side — its law is like a piece of meat salted on only one side.

This method (cutting the head and removing the brain) applies to fowl as well, except that with fowl it is customary to discard the head due to its poor quality and not cook it. But in Baghdad there is an ancient custom to bring, along with the bride as she goes from her father's house to her husband's house on the wedding night, a slaughtered and cooked rooster and hen, taking care to cook them with their heads — this being the essence of their "good sign." (The Ben Ish Chai notes its origin lies in an even older custom of bringing live chickens with the groom and bride, a sign of fertility, which was abolished after a mishap occurred in which the "king's tower" was destroyed and several people were killed, as related in Gittin 57a.) And since care is taken to cook them with their heads, one must warn that the skull bone be perforated before salting.
takeaways: Salting the head: cut in two, remove the brain, salt the brain, and salt the head inside and out (the hair does not prevent this); if only the skull was perforated, it is permitted.
Salted only on the inside, not over the hair — its law is like meat salted on one side only.
This applies to fowl too (whose head is usually discarded); in Baghdad a rooster and hen are cooked with their heads for a bride (a good sign) — so the skull must be perforated before salting.

paragraphs: Haqqulit ushear atzamot sheyyesh bahem mocha, tzerikin melicha; ak muttar lemalecham kak kemo shehem shelemim, veen tzarik leshabberam uleniqbam, ki melichat haetzem toil lammocha shebbetoko, dekocha hammelach niknas bipnim umotzi haddam, veen haetzem meakkeb. veim nitbashshel haetzem belo melicha, neesar hammocha shebbetoko, demachaziqinan dam bammocha. veim en shishshim keneged hammocha shebbaetzem, neesar hattabshil shennitbashshel immo; veim yesh shishshim, az ap hammocha muttar; abal la baenan shishshim ella raq keneged hammocha velo keneged haetzem. v"p shekkatab rama" za"l dilkattechilla lo yimlach haetzem sheyyesh bo mocha im sheer basar - katebu "hakkeneset haggedola" haggahat habbet yosep, sop ot yu"d, veah"peri chadash", saek qatan yo"d, daanachenu nohagim lekattechilla lemalecho im basar, deanu machaziqin bo dam kishar basar. veken hamminhag pashut beirenu bagdad y" lemalecham im sheer basar. uleel beparashat teharot (metzora) katabti depoh irenu bagdad y" nohagin leshabber kol haatzamot qodem melicha, veen mannichin etzem shalem.

clarification.explanation: The marrow bone and other bones containing marrow require salting, and it is permitted to salt them whole without breaking them, since the strength of the salt enters inside and draws out the marrow's blood. If the bone was cooked without salting, the marrow inside it is forbidden, and if the dish does not contain sixty times the marrow's volume, the dish too is forbidden (though sixty is required only relative to the marrow, not the bone). And although the Rema wrote that as the primary practice one should not salt a bone together with meat, in Baghdad it was customary to salt them together with the meat; and in Parashat Metzora it was mentioned that the custom was to break all the bones before salting.
takeaways: Bones with marrow require salting, even whole.
Cooked without salting — the marrow is forbidden, requiring sixty times its volume.

paragraphs: Hattelapayim hem chalulim mibbipnim, veen habbasar dabuq bekullan; lepikak tzarik lachtok meat lematta umoleach, veyannicha meqom hachatak lematta kede sheyyazub haddam, veyimlach gam mibbachutz al hassear; veyizzaher sheyyehe bechittuk zeh neqeb mammash, vetob sheyyihyeh gadol kol kak sheyyitraeh habbasar mimmennu. veim shakach velo chatak hattelapayim, umalach haregel im hattelapayim bilti chittuk: im lo bishlam adayin, yachtekem veyimlach shenit achar chittuk; veim kebar bishlam o milgem berotechim, en neesarim, dimhanne lehu bediabad otah melicha shemmillechem belo chittuk hattelapayim, vehattabshil muttar "g delekka shishshim neged hattelapayim; ukemo shekkatab maran bebet yosep, siman s"ch, dibdiabad keday hem otam rabbevata lismok alehem, ayyen sham; veken katebu gedole haacharonim za"l; udelo keharab "torat-chesed" demachmir bazeh; ken katab harab machaziq beraka, avvat d'. veraq im adayin lo bishshelam velo milgem, tzarik lachazor lemalecham achar chittuk hattelapayim kediktibena; veken hora mori harab za"l.

clarification.explanation: The hooves are hollow inside and the flesh does not adhere to all of them, so one cuts slightly below, salts, and places the cut side downward so the blood drains out (and it is good that the opening be large enough for the flesh to be visible). If one forgot to cut the hooves and salted the leg with them attached: if not yet cooked — cut them and salt again; and if already cooked or scalded in boiling water, they are not forbidden and the dish is permitted even without sixty times the hooves' volume, since after the fact one may rely on the lenient authorities.
takeaways: The hooves are cut and salted with the cut side facing down.
If forgotten and already cooked — permitted after the fact; if not cooked — cut and salt again.

paragraphs: Haavvazim vehattarnegolim, nohagim lehasir gam ken mehem rashe hatztzippareniyyim, vekannizkar b"bet-hillel". upoh irenu bagdad y", minhagam beopot vetarnegolim lachtok kol haarkubba hattachtona ad tzomet haggidim.

clarification.explanation: With geese and chickens it is customary to also remove the nail tips. And in Baghdad the custom with fowl and chickens is to cut off the entire lower joint down to the tendon juncture.
takeaways: The nail tips of fowl are removed.
In Baghdad, the entire lower joint is cut off down to the tendon juncture.

paragraphs: Im rotzeh lehabheb haopot mishshiyyure notza shebbahem qodem melicha, lo yannichem al haesh, ella yochazem beyado veyaabirem belahebet haesh henna vahenna kede lacharok shiyyure hannotza shebbahem. vetob lacharok otam al esh shel qash veteben, sheen lahem chamimut kol kak; ak nohagim lacharok "g esh shel etzim, en limchot beyadam; veraq yizzaharu shello yeshahem baachizato harbeh, ella yahapkem vigalgelem henna vahenna. upoh irenu bagdad y" nohagim lehabheb velacharok "g esh shel etzim. gam tzarik lehaddicha bet-hashshechita techilla; veken im yesh dam beayin al haop, yirchatzennu qodem hibhub. gam yachtok chutin sheyyesh ballechi. vekol zeh lekattechilla, abal bediabad im lo hedicha bet-hashshechita velo hesir hachutin, eno neesar; veraq yittol o yiqlop meqom haddam.

clarification.explanation: One who wishes to singe remaining feathers off fowl before salting should not place them on the fire, but hold them in hand and pass them back and forth through the flame to singe the feathers. It is good to singe over a fire of straw or hay, which is not as hot, but those accustomed to singeing over a wood fire (as in Baghdad) should not be protested against, provided one does not linger but keeps turning the fowl. One should first rinse the slaughter site, and if there is blood on the fowl, wash it before singeing, and cut the sinews in the jaw. All this is the primary practice, but after the fact, if one did not rinse or remove the sinews, it is not forbidden — one need only peel off the blood spot.
takeaways: Feathers are singed by holding the fowl and passing it over the flame without lingering.
The slaughter site is rinsed and blood and sinews removed before singeing.

paragraphs: Harea shel behema, sheqqorin bearbe "achamirin", nahagu leqareah veliptoach qenoqanot haggedolim shebbah, umolechin otah umebashshelim otah. veim milcho ubishshelu otah belo qeria, muttar bediabad.

clarification.explanation: It was customary to tear open an animal's lung and open its large tubes, and then salt and cook it. If it was salted and cooked without tearing, it is permitted after the fact.
takeaways: The lung's tubes are torn open, then salted and cooked.
Cooked without tearing — permitted after the fact.

paragraphs: Hakkabed shel behema, sheqqorin bearbi "svvydyn", yesh bo ribbuy dam veen lo taqqana lebashshelo al-yede melicha, ella qoreo sheti vaereb vetzolehu tzeliyya gemura, veaach"k yakol lebashshelo; ak tzarik sheyyedichennu achar tzeliyya qodem habbishshul. v"g deyesh mattirim litzloto chatzi tzeliyya - hannakon hu sheyyitzlehu tzeliyya gemura. veim yirtzeh limloach hakkabed qodem tzeliyya, yizzaher lemalecho achar shettochabo bishpud, veyitzlennu tekep, veken nohagin. veken im molecho im habbasar, yizzaher lehannicho lematta tachat habbasar velo lemala. vehamminhag lemalecho lebaddo shello im habbasar.

clarification.explanation: An animal's liver contains an abundance of blood, and there is no remedy for it in cooking through salting alone; rather it is torn lengthwise and widthwise and thoroughly roasted, after which it may be cooked (and it is rinsed after roasting, before cooking). One who wishes to salt the liver before roasting should salt it after skewering it, and roast it immediately. When salting it together with meat, it should be placed below, under the meat, though the custom is to salt it alone.
takeaways: Liver requires thorough roasting (salting alone does not suffice) before cooking.
It is salted alone, and rinsed after roasting.

paragraphs: Kabed shel tarnegolim ushear opot hu chaluq lishniyyim, vetzarik lachtok kol cheleq sheti vaereb. vezeh hakkabed yesh bo ribbuy dam, veen lo taqqana bimlicha ella raq bitzliyya. veim bishshelo velo tzelao, apillu im milcho, la mehanne leh kelum veoser kol hattabshil, vetzarik shishshim kenegdo; ak achar shetztzolehu tzeliyya gemura, yukal lebashshelo.

clarification.explanation: A fowl's liver is divided into two parts, and each part should be cut lengthwise and widthwise. It too contains an abundance of blood and has no remedy in salting, only in roasting. If it was cooked without roasting, even if salted, this accomplishes nothing, and it forbids the entire dish, requiring sixty times its volume; but after thorough roasting it may be cooked.
takeaways: Fowl liver requires thorough roasting; salting alone does not help.
Cooked without roasting — forbids the dish, requiring sixty times its volume.

paragraphs: Halleb, qoreo umolecho veaach"k yebashshelu apillu im basar. ak harbeh nohagin shello leekol leb - ben shel behema, ben shel opot mippene dimtamtem et libbo shel adam. ulepi daat rabbenu haari"y za"l gam mocha vekabed metamtemin libbo shel adam, veen leakelam; vesimanam: rashe tebot "melek". verauy shehazzekarim yizzaharu bahem beyoter shello leakelam; veken haubbarot umeniqot gam ken yihyu nizharim lebilti yoklu shelosha hannizkarim.

clarification.explanation: The heart is torn open, salted, and may then be cooked even together with meat. But many are accustomed not to eat heart at all (of an animal or fowl), since it dulls a person's heart. And according to the Arizal, brain and liver also dull the heart, and should not be eaten (with the mnemonic "MeLeKh": brain, heart, liver). It is proper for males to be especially careful about this, and likewise pregnant and nursing women.
takeaways: Many avoid heart, brain, and liver, which dull the heart (mnemonic "MeLeKh").
It is proper for males, and pregnant and nursing women, to be especially careful about this.

paragraphs: Hakkelayot ubetze zakar, dinam kishar basar, umuttar lemalecham im basar; veraq yasir haqqerumim vehechalab mehem. vehu haddin deshare litzlotam im basar.

clarification.explanation: The kidneys and the male testicles have the same law as other meat, and are permitted to be salted together with meat, only removing the membranes and fat from them. They are likewise permitted to be roasted together with meat.
takeaways: Kidneys and testicles have the same law as other meat, once the membranes and fat are removed.

paragraphs: Qurqeban sheqqorin bearbe "gantzi", veken hazzepeq sheqqorin "chotzelah" - tzerikin melicha. vehattechol, dino kishar basar. bene- meayim belo shumman shealehem, muttar lemalechah im basar; veyesh nohagin shello lemalecham im basar, vehu minhag yapeh venakon.

clarification.explanation: The gizzard and the crop require salting. The spleen has the same law as other meat. The intestines, without the fat on them, may be salted together with meat, though some are accustomed not to salt them together with meat — and this is a good and proper custom.
takeaways: The gizzard and crop require salting; the spleen is like other meat.
The custom of salting the intestines separately is good and proper.

paragraphs: Molechin harbeh chatikot zo al gab zo; v"p shehattachtona gomeret pelitatah qodem haelyona - la amerinan bolaat hattachtona min haelyona; lepi shehabbasar shoheh liplot tzir, vekol zeman sheppolet tzir, eno bolea; vaapillu shemmitqabbetz tzir veomed baggumma shebben hachatikot, muttar. mikkol maqom nohagim lekattechilla shekkol chatika sheyyesh lah bet-qibbul, mehappekin otah kede sheyyazub haddam, ubediabad en lachush. veken molechim besar op im besar behema veen chosheshin; vehaynu mittaam kevan deshoheh liplot tzir, eno bolea.

clarification.explanation: Several pieces are salted stacked one atop another, and even though the bottom piece finishes releasing its blood first, one does not say it absorbs from the piece above, since as long as meat is releasing brine it does not absorb, even if the brine collects in the crevice between the pieces. Nevertheless, the custom as the primary practice is to turn over a piece that has a concave surface so the blood can drain off. Likewise, fowl meat is salted together with animal meat without concern, for the same reason — that as long as it is releasing brine it does not absorb.
takeaways: Pieces are salted stacked together, since releasing brine prevents absorption.
Fowl meat may be salted together with animal meat without concern.

paragraphs: Betzim hannimtzaim battarnegolim achar shechita - im lo nigmar hachelbon ella raq hachelmon, tzerikin melicha kishar basar, veim kol zeh yizzaharu lemalecham lebaddam; ubediabad im millechem im basar, lo oserim velo neesarim. vekol zeh bebetzim sheen lahem ella chelmon, abal betzim shennigmeru bechelbon vechelmon, hare ellu betzim gemurot, veen lemalecham im basar ella lebaddam. v"g deshare lemalecham "g habbasar chosheshin shemma nishmatim venopelim. veim melachan im basar, neesarim kede qelippa bilbad, veyasir haqqelippa umuttarim; abal lo yukal lebashshelam qodem sheyyasir haqqelippa, ella yasir haqqelippa veaach"k yebashshelem. ubetzim ellu shennigmera qelippatam haqqasheh shennimtzeu bebeten hattarnegolet, nahagu shello leakelam bechalab.

clarification.explanation: Eggs found in a chicken after slaughter: if they contain only yolk (without a complete white), they require salting like other meat, and one must be careful to salt them separately (after the fact, if salted together with meat, they are not forbidden). But complete eggs (with both white and yolk) should not be salted together with meat but separately, and if salted together with meat, they become forbidden to the thickness of a peeling, and the shell should be removed before cooking. And eggs whose hard shell had already fully formed, found in the chicken's belly, were customarily not eaten with dairy.
takeaways: An egg with only yolk requires salting on its own.
A complete egg salted with meat — remove a peeling's thickness; a hard-shelled egg from the belly is not eaten with dairy.

paragraphs: En molechin ella bikli menuqqab, o "g qashin veqesamin, o bimqom midron, beinyan sheim yishpok sham mayim, yetzeu miyyad. vedap chalaq birhitani shehammayim zabim mimmennu, en tzarik lehannicho bemidron, abal im eno chalaq birhitani, tzarik lehannicho bemidron kede sheyyetzeu hammayim mimmennu. vaapillu bikli menuqqab yizzaher lekattechilla sheyyihyu hanneqabim petuchim; velaken lo yaamid hakkeli "g qarqa, ki zeh hu kemo keli sheeno menuqqab; umishshum hake rauy lehachmir shello limloach basar "g qarqa, vekannizkar betorat chattat, kelal y", din d', yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: Salting is done only in a perforated vessel, or on top of straw or twigs, or on a sloped surface, such that if water were poured there it would immediately run off. A smooth board from which water drains does not need to be placed on a slope, but a non-smooth board needs a slope. And even with a perforated vessel, one must be careful the holes remain open, and therefore one should not set the vessel directly on the ground (which would make it like a non-perforated vessel), and therefore it is proper not to salt meat directly on the ground.
takeaways: Salting is done in a perforated vessel, or on straw/twigs, or on a sloped surface.
One must be careful the holes remain open and not place the vessel directly on the ground.

paragraphs: Yesh machmirin qetzat lasum tok hakkeli menuqqab qash o qesamin, ki habbasar yistom hanneqabim; veen lachush kol kak lazeh; vehammachmir, t"b. upoh irenu bagdad y" minhagam limloach tok sallim haasuyim vaarugim meetzim daqqim, veniqbehem gedolim ugebohim min haqqarqa, vezeh have kemo qash veqesamin betok keli menuqqab, shei epshar lachush shehabbasar yistom hanneqabim. mihu, yesh mine kelim poh irenu sheqqorin otam bearbe "znbyl", vehem arugim meatze lulabim, vaarigatan mehuddeqet sheen nireh bahem shum neqeb lemareh enayim - asur limloach bahem; d"p sheim tannicha bahem mayim, yazub mehem - hinneh al harob yishshaer meat tzir mekunnas betok hakkeli shello yazub lematta, ubiprat achar sheyyitlachlach hakkeli hazzeh, ubiprat im yihyeh munnach "g haqqarqa.

clarification.explanation: Some are stringent to place straw or twigs inside the perforated vessel, lest the meat block the holes, and one who is stringent is blessed. In Baghdad it was customary to salt inside baskets woven from thin wood with large holes raised above the ground — this is like straw or twigs in a perforated vessel. But tightly woven vessels (called "zanbil," made from palm-frond wood) in which no hole is visible — it is forbidden to salt in them, since generally a bit of brine remains in them that does not drain, especially when they are damp or placed on the ground.
takeaways: Salt well in a perforated vessel with large holes raised above the ground.
A tightly woven vessel with no visible holes may not be used for salting.

paragraphs: Im malach bikli sheeno menuqqab, asur lehishtammesh beoto keli bedabar roteach apillu achar shehudach hakkeli. veim nishtammesh bo: im hu dabar yabesh - ben shehu nagub legamre, ben sheyyesh lo retibut qetzat - hinneh im hakkeli hu tzonen umah shehinnicha betoko cham, en tzarik ella kede qelipa, shehu shiur pachot minnetilat maqom; abal im shenehem chammin, o shehakkeli cham umah shehunnach betoko tzonen detattaa gabar - shurat haddin hu, im yesh lo retibut qetzat, tzarik netilat maqom, veim hu nagub legamre, saggi biqlipa; veayyen shalme chagiga vaperach chadash. bammeh debarim amurim? keshennishtammesh bo baddabar yabesh, abal im hu dabar lach, az shurat-haddin hu: im shenehem chammin, o dehakkeli cham umah shehunnach bo hu tzonen, baenan shishshim neged qelipa shel hakkeli. veyesh omerim: gam ledidan baenan shishshim neged shiur qelippa shel hakkeli hazzeh shemmalach bo. veim zeh hakkeli tzonen vehammunnach bo roteach, yesh omerim: ledidan deazelinan batar mera"n za"l, la baenan shishshim neged qelipa shel hakkeli; venakon lehachmir kedibrehem vekannizkar baacharonim za"l. vekol zeh shekkatabnu hu berotzeh lehishtammesh beoto hakkeli bedabar roteach, abal im yishtammesh betzonen: im hu keli-cheres, yedichennu techilla; veim eno keli-cheres, shari belo hadacha, veraq yeqannechennu heteb qodem sheyyishtammesh bo; veayyen "kareti" vesipte daat vechakemat adam ushear acharonim.

clarification.explanation: If one salted in a non-perforated vessel, it is forbidden to use that same vessel for something hot even after rinsing it. If used for something dry: if the vessel is cold and what is placed in it is hot — a peeling suffices; and if both are hot, or the vessel is hot and what is placed in it is cold — if there is moisture, the spot must be removed, and if dry, a peeling suffices. And for something moist: if both are hot, or the vessel is hot and what is placed in it is cold — sixty times the volume of the vessel's peeling is required (some say that even for us, sixty is required relative to the measure of that vessel's peeling); but if the vessel itself is cold and what is placed in it is boiling hot — some say that for us, who follow Maran, sixty is not required relative to the vessel's peeling, though it is nevertheless proper to be stringent following those who require sixty even in this case. To use it for something cold: an earthenware vessel is first rinsed, and other vessels are wiped thoroughly.
takeaways: A non-perforated salting vessel is forbidden for hot use, with various measures (peeling/removal/sixty) for other uses.
For something moist with a cold vessel and hot contents — there is a dispute whether sixty is required, and it is proper to be stringent and require it.
For cold use — an earthenware vessel is rinsed, others are wiped.

paragraphs: Im hakkeli shemmalach bo hu menuqqab: im hu keli cheres, muttar lehishtammesh bo betzonen veen tzarik hadacha, ella saggi beqinnucha heteb, abal bedabar roteach, asur apillu bediabad; veim eno keli-cheres, eno asur apillu beroteach, veraq yesh lachush beroteach lekattechilla. vekol zeh hu leiqqar haddin, abal kebar nahagu haolam shello lehishtammesh bikli shemmolechin bo apillu betzonen, uminhag yisrael tora hu, vekannizkar beshulchan gabohha, vehebio zakur letabberham, veken hamminhag pashut poh irenu bagdad y".

clarification.explanation: If the vessel used for salting is perforated: an earthenware vessel may be used for cold food without rinsing (thorough wiping suffices), but for hot food it is forbidden even after the fact; a non-earthenware vessel is not forbidden even for hot food, only as the primary practice should one be concerned. But the world has already become accustomed not to use a salting vessel at all, even for cold food, and the custom of Israel is Torah, as is also the custom in Baghdad.
takeaways: By strict law a perforated vessel is permitted for cold use.
The accepted custom is not to use a salting vessel at all, even for cold food.

paragraphs: Basar shennimlach bikli sheeno menuqqab shiur melicha liqdera, dehaynu sheeno neekol mechamat milcho, veshaha bakkeli hahu kashshiur sheyyittenu mayim al haesh veyukal leharticha, az kol mah shemmimmennu batztzir asur leakelo apillu tzali; vecheleq hachatika shechutz letzayyer, en asur mimmennu ella kede qelipa, dehaynu sheyyiqlop bammaqom shennaga bachatika shehu batztzir. vaapillu im yesh bachatika shumman, dina haki; abal im lo nimlach ella raq meat, sheen bo shiur zeh deeno neekol mechamat milcho; veken name im lo shaha shiur sheyyittenu mayim al haesh veyarticha, az gam hachatika shehi betok hatztzir enah neeseret ella kede qelipa. veayyen "peri-toar", siman tz", seip-qatan t'. vekol zeh hu ledidan deazelinan batar horaat mera"n za"l, ak bene ashkenaz hem machmirim kisbarat mvr"m za"l leesor gam hachatika shechutz letzayyer, vegam im nimlach meat veshaha meat. veayyen peri chadash, seip qatan g'. veda dildidan dela aserinan ella mah shebbetok hatztzir, hinneh im hotziu hachatika min hatztzir, velo noda ezeh tzad haya munnach tok hatztzir, veyesh sapeq shemma rob hachatika haya batztzir, az kol hachatika asura missapeq; abal im barur lanu dela haya rob hachatika batztzir, ella harob haya chutz letzayyer, veraq la yadeinan ezeh tzad haya batztzir, az kol hachatika mutteret mishshum debatel berubba, veen tzarik chad bitre, ukemo shekkatab haggaon "peleti", seip qatan t', ayyen sham. vbsh"q "rab-pealim" heerakti bs"d bitshuba bedabar zeh.

clarification.explanation: Meat salted in a non-perforated vessel with a full salting (unfit to eat due to its salt) and left there long enough to boil water on a fire — the part of the piece within the brine is forbidden even when roasted, and the part above the brine is forbidden only to the thickness of a peeling. But if salted lightly (still edible despite its salt) or not left for the required time, even the part within the brine is forbidden only to the thickness of a peeling. This follows Maran's ruling, while the Ashkenazim are stringent following the Rema, forbidding also the part above the brine. And if it is unclear which side was in the brine: if it is possible most of the piece was in the brine — it is forbidden out of doubt; if it is clear most was outside the brine — it is permitted (nullified in the majority).
takeaways: Meat left in a non-perforated vessel long enough: the part in the brine is forbidden, above it only to a peeling's thickness.
Doubt about which side was in the brine — forbidden if most was likely in the brine, permitted if most was clearly outside it.

paragraphs: Shiur hashshehiyya kede sheyyittenu mayim al haesh veyarticha, meshaarin zeh bikli benoni sheshshulayv lo ab vela daq, veken bemayim lo merubbim velo muatim, veken beesh lo merubbeh velo muat. mihu, yesh lehistappeq bekissuy: im davqa mekusseh shemmemaher leharticha, o apillu megulleh. veayyen machaziq beraka, otiyyot m"v vm"z, yeuyyan sham.

clarification.explanation: The measure of time (long enough to boil water on a fire) is measured with a medium-sized vessel whose base is neither thick nor thin, with neither much nor little water, and a fire that is neither large nor small. There is doubt whether the measure is taken with a covered vessel (which boils faster) or even an uncovered one.
takeaways: The boiling-time measure is taken with medium vessel, water, and fire.

paragraphs: "p sheshshaha habbasar shiur melicha, lo yachtok lekattechilla mimmennu besakkin qodem sheyyedichennu; vekevan shehiddichu paam achat shari lachtok mimmennu besakkin lekattechilla. ubediabad im chatak qodem hadacha, en tzarik lehagil hassakkin, veraq tzarik lahadichah; veayyen baacharonim za"l.

clarification.explanation: Even though the meat was left for the required salting time, one should not, as the primary practice, cut it with a knife before it has been rinsed; after it has been rinsed once, it is permitted to cut it with a knife as the primary practice. After the fact, if it was cut before rinsing, the knife need not be purged, only rinsed.
takeaways: Salted meat is not cut with a knife until it has been rinsed.
If cut before rinsing, the knife only needs rinsing, not purging.
